newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thief nabs Mercedes with sophisticated alarm.
newsitem.headline: Thief nabs Mercedes with sophisticated alarm.

text.p: Here's a thief who deserves some credit for ingenuity.
The Stuttgart public prosecutors' office said on Friday a man was currently on trial for stealing a pricy Mercedes 500 despite it having a sophisticated anti-theft device.
The man, according to prosecutors, disassembled the core of the anti-theft device's "black box" and replaced it with his own device that allowed him to drive the car away.
A spokesman for Stuttgart-based Mercedes, the German luxury carmaking unit of Daimler Benz, admitted it was the first time that the company had heard of the anti-theft device failing to stop a thief.
He said it was theoretically possible to disassemble the device but noted that a special computer programme would have been needed to reprogramme the new anti-theft device.
Prosecutors said the man would have needed a few months to devise the plan and sophisticated knowledge of the device.
The unidentified man faces charges for several auto thefts, according to prosecutors, who did not say when the Mercedes vehicle had been stolen. The man has denied the charges.
